title: Login, Logout, and Password Management
description: Use Django’s built‑in views and forms for authentication.

slides.title: Built‑in Auth Views 🧰
slides.content:
Django provides ready‑made views for common authentication tasks. You can use them by including `django.contrib.auth.urls` in your URLconf.

These views handle:
- Login (`LoginView`)
- Logout (`LogoutView`)
- Password change (`PasswordChangeView`)
- Password reset (with email sending)

They also come with default templates, which you can override.

slides.title: Adding Auth URLs
slides.content:
# In your project's urls.py
from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import path, include

urlpatterns = [
    path('admin/', admin.site.urls),
    path('accounts/', include('django.contrib.auth.urls')),  # includes login, logout, etc.
]

# Now you have:
# /accounts/login/
# /accounts/logout/
# /accounts/password_change/
# /accounts/password_change/done/
# /accounts/password_reset/
# ...

quizData.question: Which URL pattern is provided by `django.contrib.auth.urls` for user login?
quizData.explanation: The default URL is `/accounts/login/` when you include the auth URLs at that path.

Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `@login_required` decorator

To restrict views to logged‑in users, decorate your view with `from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required` and then `@login_required` above the view.
